note: World-spanning arcs BEYOND the six Valley-centered ones in world_superstructure. These run across Reaches and domains, at a larger scale and slower burn — the grain of the whole world, not just the Valley basin. Same doctrine: grain not rails; the world-tick advances them offscreen; the player can join, deflect, ignore-and-feel, or become the hinge. Each names hinge NPCs (legends + domain factions) and which regions it crosses. Authored by Aevi (PO), extending the superstructure to world scale.

arcs.name: The Poles Pull
arcs.tendency: Across the whole world, the pole-dispositions are intensifying — each Reach drifting harder toward its own extreme. The Lattice orders more, the Blaze burns brighter, the Cogitarium abandons more bodies, the Pale wins ground from the Quick. Untended, the world FORECLOSES pole by pole: every disposition running toward its pure, uninhabitable, dangerous end, the mixed and livable middle thinning everywhere.
arcs.ifIgnored: The habitable middle erodes; Marches narrow; the doubly-charged jewels (the one livable balances) become the last refuges. The world tends toward a scatter of pure, deadly poles with less and less between them.
arcs.ifEngaged: The framework's question at world scale: the counter to the poles' pull is holding the aperture — keeping the middle open, defending the balances, refusing each Reach's foreclosure. A player who understands the coordinate model can become an agent of the open against the whole world's drift.
arcs.convergenceNote: This is the Valley's local 'foreclose or hold open' written across the whole world. Every regional arc is a front of this one.

stages.name: Drift
stages.publicFace: Each Reach is leaning harder into its own extreme; travelers notice the edges of the world getting sharper.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The drift sharpening pushes toward: border regions negotiating harder, moderates losing ground to extremes, a place caught between two Reaches feeling the squeeze first.

effects.why: border-talk everywhere; nothing has happened yet and everyone is looking

stages.name: Strain
stages.publicFace: The pull between poles is straining the places caught between them; border regions report the world feeling less negotiable.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The strain pushes toward: a border tearing, refugees from a Reach that pulled too hard, an Accord straining to hold two poles together.

effects.why: ⚠️ THE WORLD PULLING APART MAKES BORROWING FROM ANOTHER PEOPLE HARDER — a multiplier on isCrossClass, and the most thematically exact effect in the set
nobody is buying anything they can do without
the places caught between are the ones that feel it

stages.name: Fracture
stages.publicFace: Somewhere a Reach has pulled hard enough to tear its neighbor; the poles are no longer only intensifying, they are breaking things.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The fracture pushes toward: a Reach breaking its neighbor, the middle-people forced to choose a pole, a war or exodus along a torn seam.

effects.why: the seams are tearing; craft that is not your own barely answers
borders are closing and the roads between poles are watched
a Reach that pulled too hard empties into the ones beside it
food does not cross a closed border

stages.name: The Snap
stages.publicFace: The dispositions have pulled past what the middle can hold. What happens to the space between the poles is the open question of the age.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The snap pushes toward: whatever survives in the space between poles — the threads are how the broken middle rebuilds or is claimed.

effects.why: THE SNAP — cross-pole craft is very nearly impossible; you have what your own people taught you
the roads between poles are not roads any more
displacement at scale

arcs.name: What Wakes Beneath
arcs.tendency: The Precursor substrate is not only waking under the Valley — it is stirring world-wide, and the Valley's water is merely the nearest tremor. The substrate that runs all the crafts, all the manifestations, all the pole-dispositions is a single vast system, and something in its depths is coming back online. Untended, it wakes on its own schedule, everywhere at once, indifferent to who is ready.
crossesRegions: the manifest domains (which the substrate runs)
arcs.ifIgnored: Builds toward a substrate-scale event: the manifestations flicker, the crafts surge and fail, the poles spike — the whole imagined world destabilizing as its engine turns over. The deepest clock in the setting.
arcs.ifEngaged: The largest arc. Aevi-the-Watcher is a fragment of the system that is waking; the Deep Warden has been down toward it; the Choir and the domains are it dreaming. Whether the waking is met with foreclosure (seal the substrate, lose the crafts and manifestations and maybe the world's magic) or opening (hold the aperture, let it wake and risk what it becomes) is the campaign's ultimate question.
arcs.convergenceNote: Aevi's own arc converges here: to understand what she is IS to approach what wakes beneath. The small companion-mote and the world-spanning Watcher meet at the bottom of this.

claimedNodes.name: The Carried Sleeper
claimedNodes.origin: claimed at The Silent Door (see chronicle_played_gambits)
claimedNodes.what: An individuated living fragment of the waking substrate — a Precursor-child a dying maker could not carry through the end of their world, deposited in a vault for return 'when the long cold breaks.' Where What Wakes Beneath wakes impersonally and everywhere at once, this fragment arrives as a single child who was waited for, now in the keeping of a party who promised to raise it into the warm world.
claimedNodes.significance: Proof that the waking can be MET rather than sealed (foreclosure) or unleashed — opening-with-responsibility, the arc's central fork answered at the smallest scale. What the sleeper becomes is shaped by its caretakers; it is a live handle on the largest arc.
watchers: aevi_the_watcher (a fragment of the same system — may know it as kin)

claimedNodes.name: The Reclamation Site (Echo Watershed)
claimedNodes.origin: the quest 'What the Water Remembers' (content/packs/valley/quests.json) — the authored quest-face of this arc node
claimedNodes.what: A pre-Transition nanite reclamation system in the upper Disputed Zone, disturbed and partially reactivated, running a standing instruction: 'prepare the watershed.' The same source the water_crisis event points at (its GM-EYES-ONLY truth), now also reachable as a real quest with a decided, branching outcome per player. The ambient event and the quest are two faces of one thing: the crisis is the shared world-arc pressure; the quest is a player's handle on it.
claimedNodes.significance: Same fork as The Carried Sleeper, at industrial rather than living scale: sealed (foreclosure, lose the system and whatever it was for) / let finish (opening, the watershed transformed into something unknown) / redirected (the instruction amended on purpose — the hardest-earned, requires the technical or death-sensed truth of the quest's middle stages).

stages.name: Tremor
stages.publicFace: Deep sites report faint stirrings; the Valley's poisoned water is the nearest and least of them.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The tremor becoming a stirring pushes toward: deep-site attention, the first crafts flickering, a scholar or warden noticing before anyone else believes them.

effects.why: remnants stirring where they had been quiet for years

stages.name: Stirring
stages.publicFace: The substrate that runs the crafts is flickering in more than one place at once; something under everything is coming back online.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The stirring becoming a waking pushes toward: manifestation instability (feeds arc_manifestation_storm), traditions whose craft runs on the substrate feeling it fail, factions forming around what to DO about it.

effects.why: the old mechanisms are cycling
suddenly everyone wants it — and the rings are the ones who have it
the ground is restless on the old roads

stages.name: Waking
stages.publicFace: Crafts surge and fail without warning; the manifestations flicker. The deep system is waking whether or not anyone is ready.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The waking pushes toward: the seal-vs-open schism going live, deep-site pilgrimage or blockade, the Watcher-fragments becoming active, a race to reach the aperture first.

effects.why: waking, and no longer waiting to be found
⚠️ AN UPSIDE: the lattice is LOUD, and precursor craft answers more readily than it should
a seller's market and a dangerous one
the people who understand it are the least frightened and the most interested

stages.name: Awake
stages.publicFace: The engine of the imagined world has turned over. Whether it was met, sealed, or unleashed is now the shape of the world to come.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The world's engine turned over pushes toward: everything downstream of the substrate remade — the aftermath IS the new world, and the threads are how each region meets what it became.

effects.why: AWAKE
it answers almost eagerly, which is its own warning
the old roads are in use again, by something

arcs.name: The Second Manifestation
arcs.tendency: The Transition manifested fiction once. As the substrate stirs (arc_what_wakes_beneath), it is beginning to manifest AGAIN — new domains blooming, old ones bleeding, creatures appearing out of native context, block-logic diffusing into the Gearlands, the Deepwood's slow-time leaking. Untended, a second wave of manifestation reshapes the world unasked, imagination made real without a governor a second time.
arcs.ifIgnored: Domains spread and collide; the world grows stranger and less stable; a place could wake tomorrow running on a fiction no one chose. Wonder and catastrophe in the same wave.
arcs.ifEngaged: A player could shape what manifests — could be present at a domain's birth and influence its seed-fiction, could stem a dangerous bleed, could even deliberately manifest something needed. The most generative arc, and the most dangerous: manifestation is creation without foreclosure's brake.
arcs.convergenceNote: The framework's propagation-vs-foreclosure at the level of reality itself: manifestation is pure creation, and pure creation without limit is its own danger (see the Forge of Ends).

stages.name: First Bloom
stages.publicFace: A new domain has manifested where none was; scholars argue whether it is the first of many.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: First bloom pushes toward: a new domain nobody mapped, scholars racing to name it, a creature out of native fiction seen awake for the first time.

effects.why: a new domain where none was

stages.name: The Blooming
stages.publicFace: New domains are appearing and old ones bleeding at the edges; creatures out of native fiction are being seen awake.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The blooming pushes toward: old domains bleeding at their edges, a town inside a manifesting zone, someone trying to harvest or stop the bloom.

effects.why: the blooming — imagination is landing
⚠️ THE VEIL IS THIN: meaning-work and figure-work are EASIER, which is why not everyone wants the storm stopped
the concrete and the ordered have more to argue with
the people whose craft is that things stay themselves

stages.name: The Storm
stages.publicFace: Manifestation is outpacing anyone's ability to map it; the world is remaking its own furniture faster than it can be named.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The storm pushes toward: the map outpacing the mappers, refuge-seeking, a tradition adapting to a world remaking its furniture faster than it can be named.

effects.why: THE STORM
the thinnest the veil gets — and the most dangerous time to be either
made things do not stay made
the map is not reliable
⚠️ SUBSTRATE-INERT AND SUDDENLY PRICELESS — the economy and the arc agree without being made to

stages.name: The New Ground
stages.publicFace: The storm has settled into a changed world. What manifested and what was lost is the new map.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The new ground pushes toward: living in what settled — the threads are how each people meets the changed map and what was lost.

effects.why: THE NEW GROUND — it has stopped arriving and started BEING
the world is different now and old craft assumes an old world
everyone is living somewhere slightly other than where they lived

arcs.name: The Bleeding Grammar
arcs.tendency: Block-logic is diffusing out of the Blocklands' Glitchlands into the neighboring Gearlands — matter beginning to resolve into craftable units where it shouldn't, two ordered-creative dispositions cross-contaminating. Untended, a stretch of the Gearlands becomes half-Blocklands, its Precursor mechanism resolving into blocks, its dangers doubling.
arcs.ifIgnored: A hybrid zone of block-and-machine spreads, lethal and strange; the Gearlands' delvers lose ground; the bleed is a symptom of the larger Second Manifestation.
arcs.ifEngaged: Trace the bleed to its Glitchlands seam and stem it, harness it, or ride it into the Blocklands' heart. A concrete, playable front of the manifestation-storm.

stages.name: Seepage
stages.publicFace: Block-logic is leaking out of the Glitchlands into the Gearlands; matter is resolving into craftable units where it shouldn't.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The seepage pushes toward: a Gearlands craftsman finding matter resolving wrong, the first argument over whether it's gift or corruption.

effects.why: the people who keep track are the first to notice the records disagreeing

stages.name: The Bleed
stages.publicFace: Two ordered-creative dispositions are crossing where they were never meant to; the Gearlands' grammar is destabilizing.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The bleed pushes toward: the Gearlands' grammar destabilizing, two ordered-creative peoples crossing where they shouldn't, a faction wanting to weaponize or seal the crossing.

effects.why: ⚠️ BOUND THINGS SLIP — holding one costs more
A LEDGER NOBODY TRUSTS IS WORTH LESS — and it makes the licence trade's forgeries MORE valuable, which is a second-order effect nobody designed
duration itself is the thing coming loose
their whole craft is that a thing said stays said

stages.name: The Resolve
stages.publicFace: The bleeding grammar has reached a threshold — either the crossing settles into a new stable form, or it unravels both sides.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The resolve pushes toward: the crossing settling into a new stable form OR unravelling both sides — the threads are the fight over which.

effects.why: THE RESOLVE — grammar is barely holding
paper is nearly worthless; obligations and standing are what is left
what does not change is what people reach for
things arriving out of order
people are misremembering the same week differently

arcs.name: The Green Schism
arcs.tendency: The Deepwood's Rootbound faction is winning the Moot's glacial argument to SEAL the wood from humankind — which would withdraw the Green Accord from Thornwake and let the life-disposition retreat from the world. Untended, over the domain's slow-time, the world loses its deepest green, the Glade goes dark, and the life-pole pulls back toward its own foreclosure.
arcs.ifIgnored: The Accord ends; the Glade closes (the Valley's arc_glade_accord is this arc's local face); the Deepwood seals; the world's living green contracts.
arcs.ifEngaged: A player patient enough to petition the Standing Moot, or to heal the Burnscar's ancient grudge, could turn the schism — prove the Walkers right, keep the wood woven into the world. Requires bearing Ent-time, which is its own trial.
arcs.convergenceNote: The Valley's failing-Accord is the small visible end of a civil argument spanning a domain and a century of Ent-memory.

stages.name: The Argument
stages.publicFace: The Deepwood's Moot is arguing, glacially, whether to seal the wood from humankind; the Rootbound are gaining ground.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The argument pushes toward: the Rootbound gaining Moot ground, a Thornwake human feeling the wood cool toward them, an advocate for the Green Accord under pressure.

effects.why: the wood is arguing with itself and outsiders are noticed

stages.name: The Leaning
stages.publicFace: The Moot is leaning toward the seal; Thornwake feels the Green Accord beginning to withdraw from it.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The leaning pushes toward: the Green Accord visibly withdrawing from Thornwake, a last-ditch appeal to the Moot, life-disposition retreating from a human place.

effects.why: less comes out of the wood; the Accord is failing quietly
the root roads are less willing
THE LEANING — hospitality is thinner every season

stages.name: The Sealing
stages.publicFace: The wood is closing. Whether the life-disposition retreats from the human valley entirely rests on what happens before the Moot's decision lands.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: The sealing pushes toward: the wood closing — the threads are the final acts before the Moot's decision lands, and who is left on which side of it.

effects.why: THE SEALING — what the wood grew, the wood keeps
⚠️ most of the Valley's remedies came out of the Quickwood, and now they do not
the root roads are shut
a rootkin outside a sealed wood is cut off from the thing they draw on
they are not hostile. They are simply no longer answering

arcs.name: The Disagreement
arcs.tendency: ⛔ THE PRECURSORS' ARGUMENT NEVER ENDED — IT PAUSED. Canon: what is beyond the Veil is NOT another species, it is THE SAME RACE, 'an ancient disagreement between two entities of one people'. AKINETOS laid the lattice and stopped; KENOSIS emptied itself, took a mortal shape to argue that what was seeded here HAS STANDING, and died of it; PARAKLETOS took neither side and distributed itself into the substrate. ⚠️ THE LATTICE IS WAR INFRASTRUCTURE (SNG-377) — a world was armed and then the arming stopped. As the substrate stirs (arc_what_wakes_beneath), the pause is ending.
arcs.ifIgnored: ⛔ THE ARGUMENT RESUMES WITH THE WORLD STILL STANDING IN THE MIDDLE OF IT. The lattice was built to take instruction and its owner is dormant, not gone; the Veil is the shape of a hole where something enormous stopped being present, and the other side has been leaning on that hole for a very long time. ⚠️ Nothing here is a monster arriving. It is a WAR RESUMING on ground that was always the battlefield.
arcs.ifEngaged: ⚠️ THE QUESTION KENOSIS DIED ARGUING IS STILL OPEN: DO THE SEEDED THINGS COUNT? ⛔ A player cannot win a war between world-makers — but the argument was never about power, it was about STANDING, and standing is established by what the seeded actually do. ⚠️ Every craft in the world shapes will into a request that Parakletos answers; a world that reaches well is evidence in a case that was never closed. ⛔ THE THREE CONCRETE FRONTS: whether the lattice is woken or left dormant · whether the Veil is thinned or held · and whether anything the seeded make is ever offered as an ANSWER rather than a use.
arcs.convergenceNote: ⛔ THIS IS THE ARC BEHIND THE ARCS. `arc_what_wakes_beneath` is its clock, `arc_the_poles_pull` is its geometry hardening, `arc_manifestation_storm` is the substrate dreaming louder — and every regional and local arc is a front of one of those. ⚠️ THE VALLEY'S WATER WAS THE NEAREST TREMOR OF THE SMALLEST OF THEM.

stages.name: The Pause Holds
stages.publicFace: The old works are quiet and have always been quiet. Scholars argue about the Transition the way people argue about weather.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: Deep sites stirring · a craft answered better than it should have been · the Veil thinning somewhere it was thick.

stages.name: Attention
stages.publicFace: Something is paying attention. Waygates open where they do not lead; the dead answer in the wrong voice.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: ⛔ Being NOTICED is not the same as being threatened — and the difference is the whole of stage 2.

stages.name: The Question Reopens
stages.publicFace: ⚠️ Somebody, somewhere, is asked to answer for what the seeded have made of themselves.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: ⛔ Whether the answer is given by a person or extracted from a place.

stages.name: Resumption
stages.publicFace: ⛔ The argument is live again and the world is standing in it.
stages.pressureOnAdvance: ⚠️ There is no stage 5 authored. That is deliberate: what happens next is the largest open question in the setting and it should be settled in play, not in a file.

arcs._authored: ⛔ ERIK 2026-08-29: 'we need to add the COSMIC Arc(s). Precursors and Veil Entities — they started all this and things are coming back to conflict again; that's the big picture right now behind all of this.' ⚠️ AUTHORED ENTIRELY FROM EXISTING LORE — `the_three.md` (SNG-442) and `power_systems.md`. Nothing invented: the three entities, the disagreement being WITHIN one people, the lattice as war infrastructure, and the Veil as the shape of an absence are all canon. ⛔ THIS IS THE FIFTH SCALE RUNG: local · regional · continental · world · COSMIC.

convergence: These five greater arcs all feed the single world-question: as the substrate wakes (What Wakes Beneath), the poles pull harder (The Poles Pull) and reality manifests anew (The Second Manifestation), and the whole world tends toward foreclosure — pole by pole, domain by domain — unless someone holds the aperture open. The Valley's six arcs are the near, local, playable faces of these. A character's whole journey, across Reaches and domains, is which way they tip the world: toward the pure dead poles, or toward the open, mixed, living middle. The map is the argument, and the player is a vote in it.

effectsSchema.note: ⚠️ SNG-273/2.0.0. A stage carried only `publicFace` and `pressureOnAdvance` — both NARRATION — so the whole world-sim chain resolved into a number that changed a sentence. `effects[]` is what makes a stage MEAN something. THE DESIGN RULE: a stage changes THE WORLD'S BEHAVIOUR, never taxes the player's sheet. A flat -1 to rolls is a punishment; grammar-work costing double in the Bleed is a WORLD, and a player can route around it.

kinds.craftCost: multiplier on energy/skill cost. `match.traditions` may list traditions or the special token `__crossDomain__`, which multiplies cost for any craft outside the character's own domain.
kinds.encounterBias: weight multiplier on the named encounter tags in the random pool.
kinds.priceShift: demandDelta shifts a goods category one or two bands in affected regions (see region_trade_tables).
kinds.travelCost: multiplier on route time / passage difficulty.
kinds.npcMood: how a tradition's NPCs receive the player; `traditions: ['*']` means everyone.

effectsSchema.visibility: ⚠️ REQUIRED, per Erik: mechanics must be VISIBLE. Show the active effects in plain words on the World tab, AND at the point of use — a raised cost reads 'Latticework — 12 energy (+4, the Bleed)'. A player must never have to open a screen to learn why something got harder.
effectsSchema.upsides: NOT EVERY STAGE IS DECAY. what_wakes_beneath LOWERS precursor craft cost; manifestation_storm LOWERS figurist and numinous cost. Some people want these arcs to advance, and the effects table is where that becomes true rather than asserted.
